mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes E Class 220 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: Supply-only rebuilt OM611 or OM646 engines range from £1,800 to £3,200 depending on engine code and condition. With specialist fitting, budget £2,200-£4,000 total. OM611.961 (E 200 CDI, 102 hp): rebuilt £1,800-£2,800. OM611.962 (E 220 CDI, 143 hp): rebuilt £1,900-£3,000. OM646.961 (E 220 CDI, 150 hp): rebuilt £2,000-£3,200. Labour adds £400-£800 depending on specialist location.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of 'Black Death' injector failure in an E Class 200 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Visible black, crusty carbon deposits around the injector bases under the engine cover - along with a diesel smell in the cabin or engine bay. Hard, tar-like carbon buildup around one or more injectors is the classic sign. May be accompanied by a chuffing sound from the leaking injector seal. If ignored, injectors can seize in the head, requiring specialist extraction. Early replacement of seals (£350-£550 at a specialist) prevents costly head damage.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on an older E Class 220 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the car is otherwise sound and the replacement cost is under £3,500 supply and fit. W211 E Classes still command £2,500-£6,000 used, making replacement viable. A quality rebuilt OM646 costs £2,000-£3,200 supply only. W211 examples with good service history still hold strong value. A replacement engine with warranty costs less than financing a newer car. Specialist fitting adds £400-£800, not dealer rates of £1,500+.

mainEntity.name: What causes the OM611 timing chain to fail on E Class 220 CDI models?

acceptedAnswer.text: The timing chain stretches when oil changes exceed 10,000 miles - extended service intervals are the primary culprit. Cold-start rattle is the first warning sign. Chain stretch typically occurs between 100,000-180,000 miles. Cold-start rattle that disappears after a few seconds is the early warning. Replacement at a specialist costs £750-£1,200. If the chain jumps, bent valves require a full rebuild or replacement.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the OM611 and OM646 engines in the E Class?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM646 is an evolution of the OM611 - both are 2.1-litre inline-four turbodiesels, but the OM646 features improved fuel injection pressure (1,600 bar vs 1,350 bar) and Euro 4 emissions compliance. OM611 fitted to W210 E-Class (1998-2002) - Euro 3, 102-143 hp. OM646 fitted to W211 E-Class (2002-2008) - Euro 4, 122-150 hp. Both share the same 88mm bore × 88.3mm stroke and common-rail injection. Both suffer from the same 'Black Death' injector seal and timing chain issues.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mercedes E Class 220 CDI engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance and 8,000-10,000 mile oil changes, OM611 and OM646 engines regularly reach 250,000-300,000 miles. Many examples exceed 400,000 km (250,000 miles) in taxi and fleet use. OM611/OM646 bottom ends are exceptionally robust. Injector seal replacement at 80k-150k miles is the key maintenance item. Timing chain replacement at 100k+ miles prevents catastrophic failure. Short oil change intervals (8k miles) are critical for timing chain life.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz E Class 200 CDI / 220 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The E 200 CDI and E 220 CDI badges represented Mercedes-Benz's entry-level and mid-range diesel offerings across the W210 and W211 E-Class generations. Both used closely related 2.1-litre inline-four turbodiesel engines - the OM611 in the W210 and the updated OM646 in the W211 - delivering the fuel economy and durability that made these cars UK taxi and fleet favourites.

milestones.description: **1998** - W210 E 200 CDI launched with OM611.961 2.2-litre turbodiesel, 102 hp (75 kW)
**1999** - W210 E 220 CDI introduced with OM611.962 2.1-litre turbodiesel, 143 hp (105 kW)
**1999-2000** - OM611 displacement reduced from 2,151cc to 2,148cc for E-Class applications
**2002** - W211 E 200 CDI and E 220 CDI launched with updated OM646 engine (Euro 4 compliant)
**2002-2006** - OM646 DE 22 LA fitted to W211 E 200 CDI (122 hp / 90 kW) and E 220 CDI (150 hp / 110 kW)
**2006** - OM646 updated under "EVO" name, replacing OM647 engine
**2009** - W211 production ends; OM651 replaced OM646 in W212 generation

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes E Class 200 CDI / 220 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The OM611 and OM646 engines that power the E Class 200 CDI and 220 CDI are fundamentally robust units - properly maintained examples regularly exceed 250,000 miles. However, two specific failures dominate replacement enquiries: injector seal failure ("Black Death") and timing chain stretch. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below, we break down what these failures cost to fix and when replacement is the smarter option.

problems.h4: "Black Death" Injector Seal Failure - Why E Class 200 / 220 CDI Diesel Engines Suffer Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes E Class 200 CDI / 220 CDI (OM611, OM646, 1998-2008)
problems.rootCause: The copper injector sealing washer degrades over time, allowing combustion gases to escape past the injector. This creates hard carbon deposits - the characteristic "Black Death" - that can weld injectors into the cylinder head.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Removal of injectors, cleaning of injector bores, new copper seals and stretch bolts
repairOptions.longevity: 60,000-80,000 miles; effective if caught before carbon buildup becomes severe

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Stuck injector removal (may require specialist extraction tools), thread repair, new seals and injectors if damaged
repairOptions.longevity: 100,000+ miles; necessary when injectors are seized in the head

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt OM611/OM646 with new injectors, seals and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: When injector damage has compromised the cylinder head or engine has suffered consequential damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W210 E Class 200 CDI or 220 CDI is worth £1,500-£4,000 depending on condition and mileage; a W211 example typically commands £2,500-£6,000【INDUSTRY ESTIMATE】. If the vehicle is worth under £3,000, a used engine or minor injector seal repair is usually the pragmatic choice. For W211 cars worth £4,000+, a rebuilt engine with warranty can be justified if the rest of the car is sound.
problems.recommendation: Injector seal replacement is almost always the right first step if caught early - the £350-£550 specialist cost is far less than the £2,000+ bill for a seized injector removal and head repair. If "Black Death" has been ignored and the injectors are seized, weigh the cost of head repair against a rebuilt engine. On a W211 E 220 CDI with good bodywork and transmission, a rebuilt engine often makes more sense than a costly extraction job.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM611 / OM646 Mercedes E Class 200 / 220 CDI engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch - Why OM611 and OM646 Engines Develop Cold-Start Rattle
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes E Class 200 CDI / 220 CDI (OM611, OM646, 1998-2008)
problems.rootCause: The timing chain stretches over time, particularly when oil change intervals exceed 10,000 miles. The chain tensioner loses hydraulic pressure overnight, causing a rattling noise on cold start. If ignored, the chain can jump teeth, bending valves and destroying the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: 80,000-120,000 miles; effective if caught before chain jumps and valves are intact

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chain replacement plus new valves, lifters and camshaft adjustment components
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has jumped and bent valves; requires head removal

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt OM611/OM646 with new timing components
repairOptions.longevity: When valvetrain damage is extensive or engine has seized

problems.vehicleValueCheck: (Same as above - W210 £1,500-£4,000; W211 £2,500-£6,000). On an older W210 worth under £2,500, a used engine often makes more financial sense than a valvetrain rebuild. On a W211 worth £4,000-£6,000, preventative chain replacement at a specialist (£750-£1,200) is excellent value if you catch the cold-start rattle early.
problems.recommendation: The cold-start rattle is your early warning - don't ignore it. A specialist timing chain replacement at £750-£1,200 is significantly cheaper than the £1,800+ valvetrain rebuild if the chain jumps. If the chain has already snapped or jumped and bent valves, a rebuilt engine with warranty typically offers better value than a dealer-led rebuild, particularly on a W211 with strong residual value.
